catalog_quote: [Rastorgueva 1999, p. 154, Sorkhei:] Ударение в именных частях речи и в наречиях падает на последний слог слова: estā̊ré ‘звезда’, rušán ‘светлый’, digé ‘другой’, pånjá ‘пятьдесят’, hâmišé ‘всегда’. У глаголов, не имеющих словообразующих префиксов, ударение падает: 1) в формах настояще-будущего времени изъявительного наклонения на окончание (во 2-м и 3-м лице ед. числа — на первый слог окончания): viní ‘(я) вижу’, vinénda ‘(вы) видите’; 2) в формах повелительного и сослагательного наклонения и простого прошедшего времени изъявительного наклонения — на формообразующий префикс bi-/be-/bå-: bíaw ‘принеси’, béxā̊n ‘читай’, bǻxu ‘ешь’, bávažim ‘(если) скажем’, bédiåm ‘(я) увидел’; 3) в формах прошедшего длительного времени изъявительного наклонения — на формообразующий префикс me-: mébordåm ‘(я) нес, уносил’. У глаголов со словообразующими префиксами ha-, da-, du-, va- основное ударение падает на префикс, вспомогательное — на окончание: hákennìm ‘(мы) делаем’, hákårdàm ‘(я) сделал’, dábåstàm ‘(я) связал’, dúrizìn ‘(я) лью’, váporsìn ‘(я) спрашиваю’. В отрицательных формах глагола основное ударение падает на частицу отрицания nå-, ne-: vanǻporsìn ‘(я) не спрашиваю’. [p. 165, Aftari:] Ударение обычно падает на последний слог слова: åftǻb ‘солнце’, kallé ‘голова’, širín ‘сладкий’, årū́ ‘сегодня’. [Christensen 1935, p. 34, § 35] Pour l’accentuation, les deux patois suivent en général les mêmes règles que le persan.

new_statements.translation: [Sorkhei:] Stress in the nominal parts of speech and in adverbs falls on the last syllable of the word: estā̊ré 'star', rušán 'bright', digé 'other', pånjá 'fifty', hâmišé 'always'. [...] In negative verb forms the main stress falls on the negative particle nå-, ne-: vanåporsin 'I do not ask'. [Aftari:] Stress usually falls on the last syllable of the word: åftåb 'sun', kallé 'head', širín 'sweet', årú 'today'. [Christensen:] As regards accentuation, the two dialects follow in general the same rules as Persian.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the page scan at plus the extracted text files. Rastorgueva 1999 p. 154 (article 'Surxei jazyk//dialekt', section 'Foneticheskie svedenija') reads verbatim: 'Ударение в именных частях речи и в наречиях падает на последний слог слова: estā̊ré 'звезда', rušán 'светлый', digé 'другой', pånjá 'пятьдесят', hâmišé 'всегда'', followed by the three-point verb rule (prefixless present-future on the ending, 2/3sg on the first syllable of the ending: viní, vinénda; imperative/subjunctive/simple past on bi-/be-/bå-; imperfect on me-: mébordåm), the derivational-prefix rule (ha-, da-, du-, va- main stress, secondary on ending: hákennìm, hákårdàm, dábåstàm, dúrizìn, váporsìn) and 'В отрицательных…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Sorkhei and Aftari falls on the final syllable of nouns, adjectives, pronouns, numerals and adverbs (as in Persian); verb forms are stressed morphologically: on the ending in the prefixless present, on the formative/derivational prefix (bi-/be-, me-, ha-, da-, du-, va-) otherwise, and always on the negative prefix nå-/ne-.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Rastorgueva p. 154: in prefixed verbs the main stress is on the prefix and an auxiliary (secondary) stress on the ending (hákennìm 'we make', hákårdàm 'I made'). Christensen § 36-37: the preterite ending may carry a secondary accent; with a prefix, the ending (or its last syllable) ordinarily carries a secondary accent in Sorkhei, sometimes nearly as strong as the prefix accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: prefixless present-future stressed on the ending (2/3sg on the first syllable of the ending, e.g. vinénda 'you see' vs vinnim 'we see'); imperative, subjunctive and simple past stressed on the formative prefix bi-/be-/bå-; imperfect on me-; derivational prefixes ha-, da-, du-, va- (Christensen: ha-, hi-, va-, d-, b-) take the main stress; negation nå-/ne- always takes the main stress even with other prefixes (vanåporsin 'I do not ask'; Christensen hanā́medaš 'he did not give'). Christensen: preterite of prefixless verbs stressed on the stem; mæ-/me- prefix may be stressed or unstressed; pronouns and secondary prepositions stressed or not according to diction.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (nominal parts of speech and adverbs vs verb forms); Sorkhei examples are citation forms drawn from Sotudeh's 1963 dictionary and Christensen's 1935 texts, Aftari from Morgenstierne's 1960 word material. Christensen's rules are from his own elicitation with Sorkhe informants (1914, 1929). Ezafe, conjunctions, relative ke, primary prepositions/postpositions and suffixed 'be' are unstressed (Christensen §§ 36, 38; Rastorgueva p. 150).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sork1239 'Sorkhei-Aftari' (ISO sqo) lumps two Komisenian (Semnan-belt) village dialects, Sorkhei (Sorkhe, 20 km SW of Semnan) and Aftari (Aftar, ~30 km NW). Christensen 1935 describes Sourkhéï (with Läsguerdī, itself under lasg1240-type coding in Glottolog as Lasgerdi) from informants of 1914 and 1929; Rastorgueva 1999 has separate short articles for Sorkhei (data: Sotudeh 1963, Christensen 1935) and Aftari (data: Morgenstierne 1960) plus a group article covering Sorkhei, Lasgerdi, Biyabanaki and Aftari with one stress rule. Both named varieties are covered; Aftari's own Glottolog descriptions (Borjian 2008, Homayoun 1992) were not opened.

sources.citation: Christensen, Arthur. 1935. Contributions à la dialectologie iranienne. II. Dialectes de la région de Sèmnân: Sourkhéï, Läsguerdī, Sängesärī et Chämerzådī. Det Kgl. Danske Videnskabernes Selskab, Historisk-filologiske Meddelelser XXI, 3. København: Levin & Munksgaard. 'Accentuation' §§ 35-39, pp. 34-35.
sources.note: § 35: for accentuation the two dialects (Sourkhéï, Läsguerdī) follow in general the same rules as Persian. § 36: in prefixless verb forms the preterite stresses the stem, the present (in Sorkhei) the ending (its last syllable if consonant-final); preterite ending may carry a secondary accent; suffixed forms of 'be' unstressed. § 37: prefixes ha-, hi-, va-, d-, b- and negation nä-/nå- always take the main accent; the ending then carries a secondary accent (often nearly as strong); mæ-/me- stressed or not; negation with other prefixes always keeps the main accent (hanā́medaš 'he did not give').…
